full_judgment:
The petitioners challenged two orders dated 13.11.1993 and 21.11.1993 respectively in the revision case. The petitioners by filing an application on 24.9.1991 raised the objection of limitation for executing the decree dated 31.3.1970 passed in other class Suit No. 149 of 1967. They also claimed that the execution case could nor proceed at the instance of an Indian national through an invalid power of attorney. Their further case is that they are in possession of the suit land and under the provisions of Order 21 rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure they could not be evicted by executing the decree. Therefore, they filed another application on 26.9.1991 for staying the execution of the decree. By order dated 13.11.93 both the applications were rejected. The petitioners then filed another application on 21.11.1993 under Order 21 rule 29 Civil Procedure Code for staying further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of Other Suit No. 12/88/320/85 pending in the First Court of Subordinate Judge. Mymensingh which they filed for specific performance of contract for sale of the suit land that application was also rejected on the same date. 

 2. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioners frankly submits that the objection as to limitation as raised by the petitioners is not tenable in view of the facts found in the impugned judgment. He, however, submits that the petitioner’s application under Order 21 rule 29 Civil Procedure Code for staying further proceeding of the execution case ought to have been allowed. We see no substance in this contention of Mr. Karim, for the High Court Division has rightly held that rule 29 of Order 21 applies only in case of a person who challenges the decree under execution in a subsequent suit which is not the case here. Mr. Karim then argued that the alleged power of attorney-holder was not competent to proceed with the execution case in the absence of proper validation of the power of attorney. This contention is also unacceptable because the High Court Division has held, and we think rightly, that the petitioners have no locus standi in the matter (Other Class Execution Case No. 4 of 1993).
